meta.title: Toll Bridge — tolls matched and ready to bill
meta.description: Toll Bridge pulls crossings from AutoExpreso and SunPass, matches each one to the reservation that was running at that hour and hands them to you ready to bill, with the confidence score in plain sight.

hero.lede: The crossing happens today and shows up in the portal three days later, once the car is back and the invoice is closed. Toll Bridge pulls crossings from AutoExpreso and SunPass, matches each one to the reservation that was running at that hour, and hands them to you ready to bill — with the confidence score in plain sight.

notes.body: Every crossing arrives with a number, not a verdict. 85 and up posts on its own; 60 to 84 is proposed; below 60 it stops and waits for a person.

Crossings you did bill, but to the wrong customer, that ended in a refund.

honesty.lead: We are not going to promise you a percentage.
honesty.body: How much Toll Bridge recovers depends on how clean your plate inventory is, how many bookings overlap on the same vehicle, and whether your operation crosses state lines. What we do promise: every crossing stays visible, with its confidence, and none of them bills without a human approving it.

rows.them: Someone logs into the portal, filters by date and downloads a file. Miss a week and that week is gone.
rows.us: They arrive on their own. AutoExpreso is polled continuously; SunPass in batches, with a 14-day lookback window.

rows.task: Tying the crossing to a customer
rows.them: Cross-checking plate and time against the booking calendar, line by line, coffee going cold.
rows.us: Resolved by plate, crossing time and active booking, and it comes out with an auditable confidence score.

rows.them: Solved from memory — or written off, because chasing $1.80 costs more than $1.80.

rows.them: Copied by hand onto the invoice, assuming the invoice is still open.

rows.them: Back into the portal, hunt for the crossing, and hope the receipt is still there.
rows.us: Gantry, exact time, amount and data source on the same screen as the charge. The conversation takes a minute.

rows.them: Someone's hours, every month, forever — and it grows with the fleet.
rows.us: Minutes, on the few cases that genuinely need a human eye.

how.title: Four steps, and not one of them asks you to open the portal.
how.aside: From gantry to customer invoice, without anyone retyping a single line.

steps.title: It signs into the portal for you, with your credentials
steps.body: Toll Bridge authenticates against AutoExpreso and SunPass with the account you already use and pulls the new crossings. If the portal changes shape or rejects the session, the import fails loudly and tells you — it never goes quiet pretending there were no tolls.

list.v: SunPass, in batches, with a 14-day lookback
Manual upload for any authority that isn't connected

steps.title: Every crossing lands exactly once
steps.body: Each crossing is stored with its portal identifier, so re-running an import duplicates nothing. We keep gantry, exact timestamp, plate and amount exactly as the authority published them — no rounding, no reinterpretation. That record is what you show the customer when they push back.

list.v: No duplicates even if you re-run the import
Gantry, time, plate and amount, untouched
A history of every run, including what failed

steps.title: It ties the crossing to a booking, and tells you how sure it is
steps.body: The plate says which unit crossed. The timestamp says who had it. When both line up cleanly, confidence goes up; when the crossing lands on the edge of a return, or two bookings overlap on the same vehicle, confidence drops and the case stops. The number is always visible, and you can always reassign.

list.v: Stops, with the candidates beside it

steps.title: It reaches the invoice under the policy you chose
steps.body: A matched crossing becomes a charge inside the same rental agreement where everything else already lives. You decide whether it bills at cost, with a handling percentage, with a flat fee per crossing, or drawn down from a prepaid toll package the customer bought at pickup.

list.v: A flat fee per crossing, or a prepaid package

ladder.title: What happens at each confidence level
ladder.sub: The threshold is yours: if you'd rather review everything by hand at first, push it to 100 and nothing auto-matches.

rows.title: Matches on its own
rows.body: Plate and time fall inside a single active booking, no overlaps, no edges. It moves straight to the billing queue, where you can still see it before charging.

rows.title: Proposed, and waits
rows.body: There is a likely booking but something doesn't close perfectly — the crossing landed minutes after the return, or the unit changed plates that day. We show you why, and you accept it or move it.

rows.title: It stops
rows.body: No booking explains the crossing, or two explain it equally well. We never guess who to charge: the case sits in the queue with the candidates beside it and a person decides.

disclosure.summary: How the confidence score is built, under the hood

items.def: The crossing's plate has to exist in your vehicle inventory and be valid on the date of the crossing, not just today.
The deeper inside the rental period the crossing falls, the higher the confidence. A crossing minutes from pickup or return lowers confidence on purpose.
If more than one booking could have had the vehicle at that hour, confidence drops below the automatic threshold. We would rather ask you than charge the wrong customer.
When you reassign a crossing, we record who moved it and when. The full history travels with the charge all the way to the invoice.

disclosure.note: We don't publish the exact weights because we keep tuning them with every new operation that comes on. What doesn't change is the rule: if the system isn't sure, it doesn't charge.

security.title: How we handle your portal credentials
security.aside: It's the second question everyone asks. We answer it here, before the demo.

guard.title: Handing us the portal login shouldn't feel like handing over the keys
guard.body: To pull your crossings we have to sign in where your bookkeeper signs in. That's why the access is read-only, the password never leaves the system in readable form again, and everything we do with that session is logged.

items.title: Encrypted at rest, never shown again
items.body: The password is stored encrypted and cannot be read back from the app — not by you, not by us. If you forget it, you replace it; you don't recover it.

items.title: Scoped to one operation
items.body: Each portal account belongs to a single operation inside Ride Fleet. No shared credentials between customers, or between locations that don't need them.

items.title: Read-only, always
items.body: Toll Bridge reads crossing history. It doesn't pay, doesn't top up your balance, doesn't change your portal account settings and doesn't open disputes on your behalf.

items.title: Revocable in one click
items.body: Disconnect the source whenever you want and the credential is deleted. The crossings you already imported stay; the access doesn't.

toggle.title: Toll Bridge is a module, not another system
toggle.body: It switches on inside Ride Fleet Manager and writes onto the same bookings, the same customers and the same agreements. If you ever switch it off, your imported crossings stay right where they are.

items.q: What if the customer says that toll isn't theirs?
items.a: You flag the charge as disputed from the same screen and a case opens with the gantry, the exact timestamp and the amount exactly as the authority published them. If they were right, the charge reverses and the reason is recorded. If not, you have the evidence without going back to the portal.

items.q: Can it charge the wrong customer?
items.a: It can propose wrong, which is exactly why the confidence score exists. When two bookings overlap on the same vehicle, or the crossing lands on the edge of a return, the case stops and waits for a person. And even when it matches on its own, the charge is still reviewable before it bills.

items.q: How long until a crossing shows up?
items.a: That depends on the authority, not on us. AutoExpreso publishes fast, so there we're talking minutes after the portal shows it. SunPass publishes in batches: there it's hours. Neither is instant, and anyone who tells you otherwise hasn't worked with these portals.

items.q: Do I have to use Ride Fleet Manager?
items.a: Yes. Toll Bridge matches against real bookings, vehicles and customers; without that spine there is nothing to tie the crossing to. It isn't a standalone product, and selling it as one would be selling you a prettier spreadsheet.

items.q: Can I add a handling fee on top of the toll?
items.a: Yes, and you pick the mode: at cost, cost plus a percentage, a flat fee per crossing, or a prepaid package the customer buys at pickup that crossings draw down from. What you charge is between you and your rental agreement; we just apply it the same way every day.

items.q: What happens if the portal changes and the import breaks?
items.a: It will happen — these portals change without warning. The rule is that the import fails visibly: the connection status flips, the run is marked failed and you see it on the same screen. The dangerous failure isn't a broken import; it's a silent one that makes you think there were no tolls that month.

items.q: What about old crossings, the ones from before I connected?
items.a: It depends on how much history the authority keeps: AutoExpreso lets you go further back than SunPass. Anything you can export from the portal you can upload as a file, and matching runs the same way against the bookings already in the system. If a booking from that period isn't loaded, the crossing sits in the review queue instead of attaching to the wrong reservation.

items.q: What if my fleet uses transponders, not plate reads?
items.a: It works the same way, and honestly it works better. The transponder is tied to a unit in your inventory, so the crossing arrives with the unit already identified and confidence starts higher. The only thing the timestamp still decides is who had the car at that moment.

partner.title: We're looking for design partners
partner.body: Toll Bridge is being built with real fleets in Puerto Rico and Florida. If you run tolls every day and are willing to tell us where it breaks, you come in early and your case shapes the product.

cta.title: Bring one month of crossings to the demo
cta.lede: Download your portal history, bring it along and we'll reconcile it live against your bookings. You'll see how many crossings match on their own, how many need an eye and how much money was going unbilled.
